reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point tagged as a data center in Italy is probably a mistagged professional-services office, not compute capacity.

The record carries no megawatts, no operator, no website, and no city. Its name, Studio Delta Srl, follows Italian conventions for a small professional practice, and the accompanying reading concludes the telecom=data_center tag most likely describes that office's own IT rather than a commercial facility. The determination is name-pattern based, not verified: the research status is exhausted and the firm's actual line of business was never confirmed.

For AI scaling this entry contributes nothing. A facility with zero megawatts and no operator is not a building that houses compute, and it should not be counted toward any estimate of data-center capacity or grid load. The useful signal is about data quality instead. Registries assembled from volunteered geographic tags will contain points like this one, and treating them as real facilities inflates counts without adding a single watt.

What the data does not establish is whether Studio Delta Srl operates any servers at all, or what it does. It also does not show how many similar mistags exist elsewhere, because only this one point is given. The nearest airport, Parma at 19.5 miles, is the only geographic anchor, and it says nothing about power or connectivity.
